_comment: Names that scripts/check_unwired_claims.py flags but that are not false claims.
Every entry needs a reason a reader can check, naming the intended caller or the
record that defers the wiring. An entry with a vague reason is how this gate stops
meaning anything: 'it is fine' is not a reason, 'the production loop is serve(),
Added 2026-07-26, after the Tier 0 claim inventory ran the function check for the
first time. Of the nine names it found, four were real defects and were fixed
which nothing had ever started). These five are the remainder.

2026-07-26: entries gained owner/expires, matching structural-exemptions.json and health-claim-exemptions.json. They had neither, which made every one an ETERNAL SILENT waiver - the shape this whole programme exists to remove, in the file that waives its own gate.

2026-07-30: the gate gained PART 3, manifest knobs - a config key the record offers that no Python reads. It found on_session_end's four siblings. They are waived to a NEAR expiry, not the file's usual year-end, because two of them are live UI switches and a lying switch should not sit behind a twelve-month waiver.

2026-08-18: three names the gate had been reporting on the default branch. None is a false claim - two are inversion points with no in-tree caller by design, and the third is a documented deferral the source itself states in prose. Waived rather than deleted because each is exercised by tests that pin real behaviour.

2026-08-19: the provenance store's two halves, arriving with capability doctrine step 3 (e39c2c1d). Both are implemented, fenced by RLS and pinned by a parity test that drives the Mem and PG stores through the same cases; neither has a production caller yet because the model-facing read that would mint and resolve refs is the next step of the same programme. Waived to a NEAR expiry rather than the file's usual year-end, because a deferral inside an in-flight programme should come back while that programme is still in flight. Waived by the merge pen-holder, not by their author, who was interrupted; if the intended caller differs from the one named here, correct the blocker rather than the expiry.

accept_once.reason: The single-shot attestation seam, kept for tests/integration/test_model_proxy_peer_listener_live.py. The production accept loop is `serve`, wired at fleet/infrastructure/codex_trusted_proxy_ingress.py:306, and the module docstring already says so rather than claiming otherwise. BLOCKER design: the production accept loop is `serve`, not this; nothing is waiting for a caller here and nothing should attach one.

consume.reason: Gate false positive. The code-quoted ``mcp.consume`` in api/bootstrap.py is a MANIFEST YAML KEY, not KafkaSeam.consume; the gate's dotted-prefix rule cannot tell a config path from a symbol. The function itself is a self-declaring driver seam that raises SeamUnavailable (adapters/builtin/mq_file.py:11), which is an honest unimplemented, not a false claim. BLOCKER design: this is not a deferral at all. The remedy is a gate that can tell a config path from a symbol; until then the waiver records a false positive, not an unwired mechanism.

execute_write.reason: The write half of the per-call `_Db` handed to SQL adapter handlers. The intended caller is a subclass handler (`SqlHandler`), including out-of-repo adapters; the only in-repo subclass is deliberately write_allowed=False (adapters/builtin/crm_sql.py:41). The read/write-scope refusal it guards is no longer unpinned - tests/adapters/test_sql_base_write_scope.py drives both directions through a probe subclass and proves the refusal lands BEFORE the driver, which was the part of the sentence that could quietly stop being true. BLOCKER caller: the only in-repo subclass is deliberately write_allowed=False. A subclass that sets it True is the caller that clears this.

list_all_capabilities.reason: The unfiltered admin/audit read, mandated by .vjs/logs/decisions/LOG-2026-07-17-120214.yaml and deliberately kept OFF the routing path (list_capabilities is the active-only read the router uses). Exercised by tests/integration/test_manifest_reconciliation.py; the admin surface that would consume it is not built yet. BLOCKER caller: the admin surface that would consume it. The console route module is where it would attach.

push.reason: A method of `InternalQueueAdapter`, which IS exported (boltrig/work/__init__.py) as the reference queue adapter for source integrations to copy. It is deliberately not on the `QueueAdapter` protocol, so it is outside the production contract by design rather than missing from it. BLOCKER design: deliberately off the QueueAdapter protocol, so it is outside the production contract by design rather than missing from it. No caller is intended.

sweep_run_scoped.reason: The unguarded run-scoped credential primitive. Kept, but it must NEVER be used at a run terminal: an unguarded delete of the whole run: prefix destroys a held write's sealed call, which is the record decision 0018 replays from. The terminal sweep is `sweep_run_credentials_if_settled` (kernel/held_call.py), and the prose that used to name this function was corrected on 2026-07-26. BLOCKER design: this must NEVER acquire a caller at a run terminal. An unguarded delete of the whole run: prefix destroys a held write's sealed call. The terminal sweep is a different function.

dev_principal_resolver.reason: A header-trusting resolver for LOCAL DEV ONLY: it accepts x-boltrig-* with no verification. That it has no production caller is the SAFE state and the only acceptable one, not a gap. A dev-identity build answering /v/* with no bearer was live on the internet on 2026-07-26 in a sibling estate; this waiver exists so nobody reads the gate's report as a prompt to wire it. If it ever acquires a caller outside a test, that is an incident and not a fix.

select_locale.reason: The locale-variant resolver (US-SKL-03). Nothing selects a locale yet: the loader resolves a bare base id on every path, so this is built ahead of the surface that would choose a locale. Exercised by its unit tests. The caller that clears this is a locale-aware skill selection in the loader itself.

build_cell_scope.reason: Builds a model-proxy cell scope from the child's real /proc identity for the TRUSTED lane, where SO_PEERCRED attestation is deliberately absent. The trusted-lane ingress is the module that would call it; today that path constructs its scope elsewhere. The name is reported because the gate stopped treating a package re-export as a caller ([2026] VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-WORKFLOW-PROMOTION-TRIGGER-001 D1), not because anything changed about it.

store_bearer_verifier.reason: A store-backed BearerVerifier: accepts a bearer iff its sha256 maps to an active, non-expired grant at the given generation. The proxy server currently builds its verifier by another route, so this is an alternative construction with no production caller. Reported for the same D1 reason as build_cell_scope.

select_or_generate_workflow.reason: Intent-based retrieval. The whole chain below it is unreached: this function has no production caller, `WorkflowLibrary.match` has only this one, and `learn_from_success` is gated on GENERATED_WORKFLOW_KEY, which nothing writes. Production selects a workflow by explicit id. Waived expressly by [2026] VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-WORKFLOW-PROMOTION-TRIGGER-001, whose exceptions clause names it, against the Principal question at docs/decisions/0019-route-by-intent-is-the-principals.md: should the pump route an unaddressed item by intent at all? That changes what runs for a tenant, so it is not an engineering call. On expiry without an answer the order's ratio applies with no further order: retire.

incremental.reason: memory.ingest:529 'process only new/changed content'. SURFACED IN THE UI, so an operator can toggle it and it does nothing. Sits beside on_session_end, and the MemoryIngestion receipt built for session distillation (424302f) already carries what it needs: distil only messages after the last receipt. Tracked on task #40.

bind_verb_to_agent.reason: The Python re-point API (US-KER-02). Production re-points travel the governed route instead: control.binding.set -> config/control_registry_operations.py -> control_operations.py:set_binding_record, which writes the same VerbBinding row through the approval gate. This entry point exists for in-process callers and is exercised by tests/test_verb_binding_ownership.py:59, which pins the defect that an adapter re-registering at boot must NOT silently take a verb back off a reasoning agent. BLOCKER design: two doors onto one write is the intended shape - the governed one for operators, this one in-process - so nothing is waiting for a production caller to attach here.

compose_system_prompt.reason: The layered system-prompt composition, with adversarial tests pinning that the governance floor cannot be overridden by a persona. The lane that runs today resolves a character's voice per turn instead - fleet/chat_persona.py:chosen_persona -> personas.persona_for - and sends pinned birth instructions resolved once at import. prompt_stack's other exports ARE wired (wrap_untrusted in chat_turn_execution.py, compose_tool_harness at fleet/infrastructure/codex_kernel_tools_phase.py:54); only this one is not. The source says so in its own prose at prompt_stack.py:81 and chat_persona.py:5, so the record does not claim otherwise, and the remaining wiring is recorded as SOUL-1 (DEPENDS-BACKEND) in docs/design/surfaces/agent-builder.md.

register_persona.reason: The out-of-tree character hook, called at import by a private bundle that is not in this repository - the same inversion as a manifest module_ref resolving an adapter's build() factory, which reachability-roots.json already records for the cloud_audio builders. It lives in the hand-written personas.py precisely so a regeneration of the GENERATED personas_shipped.py cannot destroy it (personas_shipped.py:7-9). Its refusals - a blank id, a blank system prompt, and overwriting a shipped character - are pinned by tests/test_chat_persona.py:244-257. BLOCKER design: an in-tree caller would defeat the point, since the hook exists so a private character need not be shipped inside the kernel container.

observe_entities.reason: The minting half of the opaque record ref. Records a sighting and returns brref_<type>_<opaque>, deterministic through a unique index rather than derivation - e39c2c1d explains why a derived ref would be an offline confirmation oracle. Exercised by tests/store/test_provenance_store_parity.py, which drives Mem and PG through identical cases, and composed into CapabilityRoutingStore (boltrig/store/capability_routing.py:82,158) so the seam is reachable rather than orphaned. BLOCKER caller: the model-facing capability read that would record a sighting is doctrine step 3/4 work and is not built; agent_capabilities.py is where it would attach.

resolve_entity_ref.reason: The resolving half, and the record already names it as mandatory rather than optional: boltrig/models/provenance.py:83 says it 'is the only thing that answers' whether a ref exists, belongs to this tenant and points anywhere, and that a positive is_ref() is never authorisation to skip it. So this is a deferred CALLER, not a false claim - the prose that defers it is in the tree and checkable. Exercised by tests/store/test_provenance_store_parity.py. BLOCKER caller: the same unbuilt model-facing read as observe_entities; the two land together or neither does.
